analysis:
I examined the BASE text for MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift (lines 529-1657): the media/vision path, the text submit path, makeDeadlineCheckedEventStream, makeEventStream, prepareNativeMiMoMedia, tokenize/detokenize/applyTemplate and resolveTokenizer.

The patch excerpt shows a new head guard at 512-519. It rejects GLM media requests when GLM5NextPromptPolicy.withholdsOutput holds (required/named tool_choice or JSON response_format). This fails closed with invalidToolPayload after releaseBox.fire(), so the model pin is not leaked.

Head 985-1006 adds withholdsGLMOutput, which forces a native reasoning prefix and native channel routing for GLM text requests that withhold output. That separates reasoning into a typed channel.

Other head changes (1126, 1153, 1187, 1231-1241, 1300-1302, 1309, 1419, 1470, 1490-1493, 1590, 1597-1598) are not visible as head text. They map to base yield sites in makeEventStream at 1279-1282, 1392-1395, 1446-1448 and 1570, so they likely add GLM withholding or validation before events are yielded.

Integration must verify on the head side that:
(1) withheld GLM JSON or forced-call output is never yielded before ToolConstraintValidation and formatOutput.validate succeed, including the error, cancellation and terminal paths;
(2) withheld reasoning is accounted through usageSignal.recordWithheldReasoning consistently, so billing is not affected;
(3) no path drops releaseBox.fire or cancelUpstream.

No cache-scope changes are visible. requestCacheScope is still passed to submitTokenized, and native MiMo media keeps cacheEnabled:false, so T-041 salt plumbing appears unchanged.

No security regression was identified from the visible evidence. Head-side coverage of the makeEventStream changes is a limit of this review, not evidence that they are safe.
